subject: general
question: Sometimes after doing physical work we get muscle cramps. This results due to

options.text: non-conversion of glucose to lactic acid.
conversion of pyruvate to lactic acid.

solution:
__**Concept:**__

__
 
• Muscle cramps happen when **anaerobic respiration** takes place in our muscle cells.
 
• When we are doing **heavy physical work/exercise then there is a lack of oxygen as demanded by the muscles cause this.**

**Explanation:**__

The below figure explains the flow of conversion of glucose to energy -

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3f0e5b123197bf561e92a4be70959fc06cc58bb19d3ebe2eacc03e2358bcdf60.png] 

 
• When the **Pyruvate converted into lactic acid **instead of CO₂ + Energy + H₂O
 
• Muscle cramps occur.
 
• A **hot water bath or a massage can help in getting relief from muscle cramps.** These two things improve blood circulation, thereby increasing the supply of oxygen to the muscles.

**Hence, after doing physical work we get muscle cramps are due to the conversion of pyruvate to lactic acid.**
